Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A normalised, production-standard PostgreSQL schema forms the transactional source of truth for the platform. \\ * Core tables (accounts, instruments, orders, positions) are created with keys, constraints and indexes. \\ * The schema is version controlled as migration files and every team member can explain the model. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * This is the data foundation every later component builds on; it converges on contracts/database-schema.sql. \\ * Returning-intern run: fundamentals of business software development are recapped inside this sprint, not taught from scratch. \\ * Historical trade structures are delivered as a documented design here, not a built implementation. \\ * Snowflake is introduced as the analytics warehouse Postgres will later feed. \\ * Security focus: parameterised queries (OWASP A03), schema constraints, least-privilege DB roles, no secrets in connection config.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Entities, attributes and relationships for the trading domain are identified. \\ * An entity-relationship diagram documents accounts, instruments, orders and positions. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Identify the core entities (Account, Instrument, Order, Position) and their relationships. \\  \\ Model cardinality and optionality between entities. \\  \\ Commit the ER diagram alongside a short data dictionary. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Every team member must be able to walk the diagram unaided at showcase.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The schema is normalised to third normal form with no redundant or transitive dependencies. \\ * Any deliberate denormalisation is documented with rationale. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Translate the ER diagram into a normalised relational design (1NF, 2NF, 3NF). \\  \\ Document any justified denormalisation for query performance. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Third normal form is mandatory for this run and is not traded away for time.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * ACCOUNTS, INSTRUMENTS, ORDERS and POSITIONS tables exist with correct column types. \\ * Primary keys, foreign keys, unique constraints and check constraints enforce integrity. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create the ACCOUNTS table (id BIGINT PK, account_id VARCHAR UNIQUE, holder_name, cash_balance NUMERIC(18,2), status, version, last_updated). \\  \\ Create the ORDERS table (id UUID PK, account_id FK, symbol FK, side, quantity, price, status, idempotency_key UNIQUE, created_on). \\  \\ Create INSTRUMENTS (symbol PK, name, asset_class, currency, tradable) and POSITIONS (account_id FK, symbol FK, quantity, average_cost). \\  \\ Add check constraints (quantity > 0, price > 0, status enumerations) and a unique constraint on idempotency_key. \\  \\ Capture the DDL as version-controlled migration files so the database can be recreated. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The unique constraint on idempotency_key is mandatory; the executor depends on it in Sprint 7. \\ * Use least-privilege roles for the application connection; no superuser credentials in config.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * At least three indexes support the common access patterns, each justified by a named query. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add indexes on ORDERS(account_id, created_on) and POSITIONS(account_id, symbol) and lookups by symbol. \\  \\ Verify index usage with EXPLAIN on the representative queries.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A documented design covers how historical trade records are retained alongside the live operational tables. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Design structures to retain historical trade records for analytics and audit. \\  \\ Document how historical data would be populated and queried. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Reduced for this run to a documented design rather than a built implementation.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Seed data loads with one command and covers active, suspended and closed accounts. \\ * Representative accounts, instruments, orders and positions are queryable and referentially intact. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Author a seed-data script inserting realistic accounts, instruments and trades. \\  \\ Confirm referential integrity holds after loading. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Seed data must be rich enough to support the Sprint 4 analytics work.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A Python dashboard surfaces at least three business insights over a realistic trading dataset. \\ * Ingestion is structured as a testable extract, transform, load pipeline. \\ * Data is accessed through the Fauxnance API, orienting teams to the operational versus analytical split. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * First orientation to the Fidelity data landscape (operational Postgres versus analytical Snowflake). \\ * The dataset must include at least two NSE or BSE instruments so the cohort trades a market they know. \\ * The Fauxnance key is read from the environment, never committed, and the browser never calls Fauxnance. \\ * Security focus: validation and data-quality checks (OWASP A08), safe handling of sensitive financial data, pytest guards.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A realistic sample trading dataset is added, including at least two NSE or BSE instruments. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Source or generate a representative dataset covering trades, accounts and instruments. \\  \\ Include Indian symbols such as INFY.NS, RELIANCE.NS or TATASTEEL.BO alongside the others. \\  \\ Document the dataset schema and provenance.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Patterns, anomalies and segments are explored and summarised. \\ * Missing values, incorrect types, malformed dates and outliers are handled explicitly. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Load the dataset with pandas and profile distributions, ranges and null patterns. \\  \\ Implement cleaning transforms for missing values, type coercion, date parsing and outlier treatment. \\  \\ Record every cleaning decision so results are reproducible. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Merged for this run: returning interns hold the pandas basics, so profiling and cleaning ship as one applied task.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * At least three business insights are produced, each stated as a claim a non-technical reader can follow. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Compute trade volume (count and value by date). \\  \\ Identify the most active accounts and the fill rate (filled versus rejected). \\  \\ Compute exposure by instrument and average trade size over a period.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Clear, well-labelled charts communicate the insights to a non-technical audience. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Select appropriate chart types for each insight (matplotlib, seaborn or plotly). \\  \\ Assemble the charts into a simple dashboard view.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Ingestion is separated into distinct extract, transform and load functions. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Structure ingestion into extract, transform and load stages. \\  \\ Load prepared data into the analytical store for reporting. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * ETL is introduced conceptually here; the depth comes in Sprint 7.

Summary: Access Fauxnance Data Through a REST API
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Candle data is pulled through the Fauxnance API with the key read from the environment. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Call GET /candles/{symbol} with the X-Api-Key header read from the environment. \\  \\ Handle rate-limit (429) and error responses gracefully, not with a bare try block. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Fauxnance gives a 2000-requests-per-day quota per key; batch and cache to stay inside it.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * pytest validates the pipeline transforms and catches bad data early. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write unit tests for the transform functions, including one malformed-input case. \\  \\ Add validation tests that fail on out-of-range input. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid input transforms to expected output \\ # missing required field is rejected \\ # out-of-range value is flagged \\ # empty dataset handled without error

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A dimensional model for trade analytics is defined in the analytical store. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Define DIM_ACCOUNT, DIM_INSTRUMENT, DIM_DATE and FACT_TRADES. \\  \\ Document the star schema and its grain. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * This schema is the load target for the Sprint 7 batch pipeline. \\ * Teams without a Snowflake account use DuckDB; contracts/analytics-schema.sql runs on either.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The core trading engine is designed with UML and built in clean, SOLID, unit-tested Java 21. \\ * Domain entities, enumerations, DTOs and a custom exception hierarchy model the trading domain. \\ * Order placement and settlement logic is standalone, with no database, HTTP or Spring dependency. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Pure domain logic; this is the business-logic engine the Sprint 6 service will expose. \\ * Core Java is a refresher for this run; tests are still written before implementation, evidenced in commit history. \\ * Security focus: input validation in the domain model, defensive coding, clean code to minimise the vulnerability surface.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * UML class and sequence diagrams model the trading domain and order lifecycle, and match the code. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Identify entities, responsibilities and relationships from the requirements. \\  \\ Produce class diagrams (association, aggregation, composition, inheritance). \\  \\ Produce sequence diagrams for order placement and settlement. \\  \\ Peer-review the diagrams and refine.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Account, Instrument, Order and Position entities are implemented in Java and match the domain model. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create Account (id, accountId, holderName, cashBalance, status, version, lastUpdated) with debit(), credit(), isActive(). \\  \\ Create Instrument (id, symbol, name, assetClass, currency, tradable) with isTradable(). \\  \\ Create Order (id, accountId, symbol, side, quantity, price, status, idempotencyKey, createdOn). \\  \\ Create Position (accountId, symbol, quantity, averageCost) with apply() and marketValue(). \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * accountId means the numeric ACCOUNTS.id everywhere; the string business identifier is ACCOUNTS.account_id only.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * AccountStatus, OrderSide and OrderStatus enums match the specification exactly. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create AccountStatus (ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, CLOSED). \\  \\ Create OrderSide (BUY, SELL) and OrderStatus (NEW, FILLED, REJECTED, CANCELLED).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Request and response DTOs carry validation annotations. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create PlaceOrderRequest with @NotNull and @Positive validations. \\  \\ Create OrderResponse, AccountResponse, PositionResponse and ErrorResponse. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid request passes validation \\ # null required field is rejected \\ # non-positive quantity or price is rejected

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A custom exception hierarchy covers all six specified error conditions. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create AccountNotFoundException and AccountNotActiveException. \\  \\ Create InstrumentNotFoundException. \\  \\ Create InsufficientFundsException and InsufficientHoldingsException. \\  \\ Create DuplicateOrderException for reused idempotency keys.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Business rules 1 to 8 are enforced in the domain, and positions and cash update atomically. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement order validation (account exists and is ACTIVE, instrument tradable, quantity and price > 0). \\  \\ Implement BUY logic: verify cash balance >= quantity x price, then debit cash and update position. \\  \\ Implement SELL logic: verify held quantity >= order quantity, then credit cash and reduce position. \\  \\ Enforce idempotency using the idempotency key. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # buy succeeds and updates cash and position \\ # buy rejected on insufficient funds \\ # sell rejected on insufficient holdings \\ # order rejected on inactive account \\ # order rejected on unknown or non-tradable instrument \\ # duplicate idempotency key rejected

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Domain logic is covered by meaningful JUnit tests written test-first (red, green, refactor). \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write AccountTest: testDebit_Success, testDebit_InsufficientFunds, testCredit_Success. \\  \\ Write OrderLogicTest: testBuy_Success, testSell_InsufficientHoldings, testReject_InactiveAccount. \\  \\ Write PlaceOrderRequestValidationTest: testValidRequest, testInvalidQuantity, testNullFields. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A single unit test is one class, one method, one execution path; cover error paths as isolated tests.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Sprint 5 logic is wrapped in a layered, Dockerised Spring Boot service with MyBatis persistence to Postgres. \\ * All six endpoints implement contracts/trade-api.yaml, including the error envelope and every code in the catalogue. \\ * A protected route is authenticated against the provided Node auth stub. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * First service exposing the core logic via an API; OpenAPI-first is assessed against the provided contract, not one authored from scratch. \\ * GitHub Copilot is introduced in this sprint; teams keep a short code-walkthrough note explaining any Copilot-generated code they keep. \\ * The Node auth stub is a provided fixture (issuer auth-stub, port 3000, shared dev secret); the real Auth service replaces it in Sprint 8. \\ * Security focus: JWT validation on protected endpoints, Bean Validation on DTOs, safe error handling with no stack-trace leakage (OWASP A01, A05).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A Spring Boot project is bootstrapped with the required dependencies and configuration. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create the Spring Boot project and add web, validation, MyBatis and OpenAPI dependencies. \\  \\ Configure application properties (datasource, server port, logging).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service implements contracts/trade-api.yaml for the order and account endpoints. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Read contracts/trade-api.yaml and map POST /api/v1/orders, DELETE /api/v1/orders/{id} and the account endpoints. \\  \\ Match the request and response schemas and the error envelope to the provided contract. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Design is assessed against the provided contract; the team does not author the contract from scratch.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service follows a clean controller to service to repository layering; no SQL in a controller, no HTTP type in the domain. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Establish controller, service and repository layers with clear responsibilities. \\  \\ Wire dependency injection between the layers.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * MyBatis mappers persist and query against the Sprint 3 Postgres schema using parameterised statements throughout. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement MyBatis mappers for accounts, orders and positions. \\  \\ Use parameterised statements throughout to prevent injection. \\  \\ Map result sets to the domain and DTO objects. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # order row inserted and retrievable \\ # account and positions read correctly \\ # mapper throws on constraint violation

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * OrderService wraps the core logic with transactional order processing and optimistic locking. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement placeOrder(PlaceOrderRequest), cancelOrder(orderId), validateOrder() and executeOrder(). \\  \\ Annotate order placement with @Transactional so cash and position update atomically. \\  \\ Apply optimistic locking using the account version column. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # place order commits cash and position together \\ # failed order rolls back with no partial write \\ # concurrent update detected via optimistic lock

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * AccountService exposes account, balance, positions and order-history reads. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement getAccount(id), getBalance(id), getPositions(id) and getOrders(id). \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # account details returned for valid id \\ # not-found error for unknown account

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * POST /api/v1/orders places an order and DELETE /api/v1/orders/{id} cancels a working order. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement POST /api/v1/orders returning orderId, status and echo of the order. \\  \\ Implement DELETE /api/v1/orders/{id} returning the updated order status. \\  \\ Return ORD-409 when cancelling a filled or already-cancelled order. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # request mapping invalid (400) \\ # server error (500) \\ # order placed and filled successfully \\ # order rejected on business-rule failure \\ # working order cancelled successfully \\ # cancel of filled order returns conflict \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Test the place and cancel flow using the real controller, service and MyBatis persistence against Postgres.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * GET endpoints expose account details, cash balance, positions and order history. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement GET /api/v1/accounts/{id}, /balance, /positions and /orders. \\  \\ Shape responses via the account and position DTOs. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # request mapping invalid (400) \\ # server error (500) \\ # account, balance, positions and orders returned successfully \\ # unknown account returns not found \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Test the read flows using the real controller, service and persistence classes.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Incoming requests are validated with Bean Validation and responses are shaped by DTOs. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Apply @Valid and Bean Validation constraints on request DTOs. \\  \\ Return VAL-422 for invalid input. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid request accepted \\ # invalid quantity or price returns 422 \\ # null required field returns 422

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A @ControllerAdvice maps every domain exception to its documented code and status with no stack-trace leakage. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement @ControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler methods. \\  \\ Map exceptions to ACC-404, ACC-403, INS-404, ORD-400, ORD-409, VAL-422 and AUTH-401 with the correct HTTP status. \\  \\ Return the ErrorResponse shape and log the error internally without exposing internals. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # account not found maps to ACC-404 (404) \\ # inactive account maps to ACC-403 (403) \\ # insufficient funds maps to ORD-400 (400) \\ # duplicate order maps to ORD-409 (409) \\ # invalid input maps to VAL-422 (422)

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service emits structured logs suitable for auditing order activity. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add structured logging around order placement, cancellation and errors. \\  \\ Ensure no secrets or sensitive payloads are logged.

Summary: Integrate the Provided Node Auth Stub
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A protected route validates a real JWT issued by the provided Node auth stub and rejects a missing or invalid token with AUTH-401. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add a Spring Security filter that validates the stub's JWT (issuer auth-stub, shared dev secret) on protected routes. \\  \\ Reject a token whose accountId claim does not match the addressed account with ACC-403. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The stub is a fixture with no tests to write; the real NestJS Auth service replaces it in Sprint 8 with a configuration change only.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service runs as a Docker image built with a multi-stage Dockerfile. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write a multi-stage Dockerfile that builds and packages the service. \\  \\ Verify the containerised service starts and serves requests.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Three Kafka topics with producers and consumers move trade events per contracts/kafka-topics.md. \\ * The Trade Executor consumes orders, prices against a live Fauxnance quote, applies fill or reject rules, updates order, cash and position in one transaction, and publishes to trade-events. \\ * A market-data poller publishes Fauxnance quotes to the market-data topic, and a batch ETL loads FACT_TRADES. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * There is no Broker Simulator: the team builds the Trade Executor and the fill logic themselves. \\ * Monday is a public holiday (Ganesh Chaturthi), so this is a four-taught-day week; scope the executor and ETL work accordingly. \\ * The duplicate-delivery demonstration (a replayed message must not double-debit an account) is mandatory. \\ * Copilot is available; keep a short code-walkthrough note for any generated executor or poller code kept. \\ * Security focus: DevSecOps in CI (SAST, dependency scanning, secret detection) and SonarQube quality gates (OWASP A06, A08).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The orders, trade-events and market-data topics are created with documented keys and partition counts. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create orders and trade-events keyed by accountId with three partitions each. \\  \\ Create market-data keyed by symbol with six partitions. \\  \\ Document the five-field envelope (eventId, eventType, eventTime, source, schemaVersion) and the rationale for each key and partition count.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Trade REST API publishes ORDER_PLACED to orders and returns NEW; lifecycle outcomes are published to trade-events. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Change POST /api/v1/orders to record the order, publish ORDER_PLACED to orders, and return NEW. \\  \\ Publish ORDER_FILLED, ORDER_REJECTED and ORDER_CANCELLED to trade-events from the executor. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # ORDER_PLACED published on a newly accepted order \\ # producer handles broker-bus unavailability without losing the order \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * From this sprint the endpoint returns NEW and the fill arrives on trade-events; the UI must handle both NEW and synchronous FILLED.

Summary: Trade Executor: Marketability Gate & Fill Logic
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Trade Executor consumes orders, prices each against a live Fauxnance quote, applies the fill or reject rule, and writes the outcome in one transaction. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Consume the orders topic in a single consumer group. \\  \\ Fetch a live quote from Fauxnance GET /quotes/{symbol} for the order symbol. \\  \\ Apply the marketability gate: fill the whole order at the quote when a BUY limit is at or above the quote, or a SELL limit is at or below it; reject otherwise. \\  \\ Re-check funds and holdings at execution time before committing, since state may have changed since acceptance. \\  \\ Update order, cash and position in one transaction, then publish ORDER_FILLED or ORDER_REJECTED to trade-events. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # buy limit at or above quote fills at the quote \\ # sell limit at or below quote fills at the quote \\ # order outside the marketable range is rejected \\ # execution-time funds re-check rejects an order that no longer has cash \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Test the executor against a mocked Fauxnance quote source covering fill, reject and pricing-unavailable responses. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Partial fills are out of scope: the order status enumeration has no state for them.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Consumption is idempotent against redelivery and a replayed message does not double-debit an account. \\ * Malformed or unprocessable messages are routed to a dead-letter queue without stalling the partition. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Key idempotency on the envelope eventId so a duplicate delivery is a no-op. \\  \\ Commit the offset only after the side effect is durably written. \\  \\ Route messages that fail deserialisation or validation to a dead-letter queue and continue. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # event consumed and processed once \\ # duplicate delivery handled idempotently with no double-debit \\ # malformed message routed to dead-letter and consumer continues

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A poller calls Fauxnance on an interval and publishes each quote to the market-data topic keyed by symbol. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Call GET /quotes?symbols=A,B,C batching up to 25 symbols per request. \\  \\ Publish each quote to market-data keyed by symbol. \\  \\ Poll only held and watched symbols and cache, to stay inside the 2000-requests-per-day quota. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # batch of up to 25 symbols fetched in one request \\ # each quote published keyed by symbol \\ # poller stays within the daily quota under a held-symbol set \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * This poller is what creates the real-time stream the Sprint 10 Watchlists and Portfolio extensions consume; the key stays in the environment.

Summary: Batch ETL: Incremental Load to Snowflake
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A single incremental load moves trade data from Postgres into FACT_TRADES and its dimensions, with dead-letter handling for bad rows. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement extract, transform and load stages for trade data. \\  \\ Load FACT_TRADES and the dimension tables defined in Sprint 4 as an incremental load. \\  \\ Route rows failing validation or schema checks to a dead-letter store without killing the load. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # incremental load populates FACT_TRADES \\ # transform handles nulls and type mismatches \\ # invalid row routed to dead-letter and the load continues \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Reduced for this run to a single incremental load rather than the full-plus-incremental pipeline.

Summary: Characterisation Tests on Own Sprint 6 Code
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Characterisation tests capture the existing behaviour of the team's own Sprint 6 code before it is extended. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write characterisation tests around the Sprint 6 Trade REST API code. \\  \\ Apply the first refactors (extract method, replace conditional, introduce parameter object) with tests proving behaviour is unchanged. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The india branch ships clean stubs, so the refactoring subject is the team's own code, not a planted starter codebase.

Summary: SonarQube Quality Gates & DevSecOps in CI
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * SonarQube analysis and DevSecOps checks run in CI and the quality gate passes on the pipeline and the Java services. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Wire SonarQube analysis into GitHub Actions and interpret the findings. \\  \\ Add SAST, dependency scanning and secret detection to CI. \\  \\ Configure quality gates that fail the build on a threshold breach.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The analytics dashboard reads from both the real-time stream and the batch warehouse and reconciles the two. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Extend the Sprint 4 dashboard to read real-time and batch sources. \\  \\ Reconcile the two views for consistency.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A centralised NestJS Auth service implements contracts/auth-api.yaml, hashing credentials in Postgres. \\ * Swapping the stub for the real service protects at least one Trade REST API route end to end with a configuration change only. \\ * The auth flow is reviewed against the auth-focused OWASP items, with live OpenAPI docs served by the running service. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The security keystone of the platform. \\ * Two SME sessions run on Monday and Tuesday, so plan the deliverable around the remaining build days. \\ * Refresh-token rotation is reduced to issuing a new refresh token on each refresh; revoking the previous one is optional and documented if not built. \\ * Security focus: password hashing, JWT issuance and validation, defence against token leakage, replay and timing attacks (OWASP A07, A01).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A modular, layered NestJS service is scaffolded in TypeScript with controller, service and repository layers. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Scaffold the NestJS project with modules, controllers and providers. \\  \\ Establish the layered structure and dependency injection.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The auth endpoints implement contracts/auth-api.yaml before implementation detail is filled in. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Map the login, register and refresh endpoints to the provided contract. \\  \\ Match the token and error response schemas to the contract.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Auth service exposes register, login and refresh endpoints, and refresh issues a new refresh token each time. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement register(), login() and refresh() in AuthService. \\  \\ Validate inputs with class-validator and class-transformer. \\  \\ On refresh issue a new refresh token; document whether the previous one is revoked. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # request mapping invalid (400) \\ # server error (500) \\ # registration succeeds for a new user \\ # registration rejected for an existing user \\ # login succeeds and returns a token \\ # login fails on bad credentials \\ # refresh issues a new token for a valid refresh token \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Test register, login and refresh against the real service and Postgres persistence.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Passwords are hashed with argon2 or bcrypt using per-user salts; plaintext is never stored or logged. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Hash credentials with argon2 or bcrypt and store only the hash and salt. \\  \\ Verify passwords using a constant-time comparison. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # correct password verifies \\ # incorrect password fails verification \\ # weak hashing (MD5 or SHA) is not used

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A signed JWT is issued on login with claims that exactly match the contract: sub, accountId, roles, iat, exp. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement TokenService.issue() building a signed token (header, payload, signature). \\  \\ Set expiry and the required claims; sign with a securely managed secret. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # token issued with the contract claims and expiry \\ # token signature verifies with the service key

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Tokens are validated on protected routes and rejected with AUTH-401 when invalid or expired. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement TokenService.verify() and decode(). \\  \\ Reject expired, tampered or malformed tokens with AUTH-401. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid token accepted \\ # expired token rejected \\ # tampered signature rejected \\ # malformed token rejected

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Guards protect routes and a decorator extracts the authenticated user from the token. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement an auth guard on protected endpoints. \\  \\ Add a decorator that extracts the user from the validated token. \\  \\ Add interceptors as needed for the request lifecycle. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # guard blocks an unauthenticated request \\ # guard allows an authenticated request \\ # user correctly extracted from the token

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service uses structured logging (winston or pino) without logging sensitive data. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add structured logging around auth events. \\  \\ Ensure credentials and tokens are never written to logs.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The auth flow is reviewed against the auth-specific OWASP items and hardened. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Review for broken authentication and broken access control (OWASP A07, A01). \\  \\ Ensure a failed login gives the same response and timing for an unknown user as for a wrong password. \\  \\ Assess and mitigate token leakage, replay, weak secrets, and document the findings.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Jest tests cover the service, the guard and token handling, including the expired-token and wrong-signature paths. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write unit tests mocking providers and testing the guard. \\  \\ Cover token issuance, validation and error paths. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # guard unit test blocks and allows correctly \\ # token issuance produces a valid token \\ # validation rejects expired and tampered tokens

Summary: Replace the Stub and Protect a Spring Boot Route End-to-End
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Sprint 6 stub is swapped for the real Auth service so at least one Spring Boot route is protected end to end, with no code change in the Trade REST API beyond configuration. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Point the Trade REST API at the real Auth service by configuration only. \\  \\ Publish live OpenAPI docs served by the running Auth service. \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Obtain a token from the Auth service, call a protected Spring Boot route, and confirm rejection without a valid token.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Angular frontend delivers an authenticated login flow end to end and the core trading views. \\ * The UI consumes the Trade and Auth REST APIs via clients generated from contracts/, not hand-written. \\ * Core journeys are covered by unit tests and a reduced Playwright suite; no secret is present in the built bundle. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * User-facing app; with this the full stack is complete. \\ * Friday is a public holiday (Gandhi Jayanti) and self-directed SRE content runs on Monday, so this is a compressed week; scope the views accordingly. \\ * The Playwright suite is reduced to the login and place-order journeys for this run. \\ * Security focus: JWT interceptors attach bearer tokens, route guards protect authenticated routes, output encoding prevents XSS (OWASP A03, A01).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Angular app is scaffolded with standalone components, routing and signals. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create the Angular project with standalone components and routing. \\  \\ Set up the build tooling and dev server.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Users can log in, the token is stored, and a JWT interceptor attaches it to Trade and Auth API calls only. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement AuthService with login(), logout(), isAuthenticated() and getToken(). \\  \\ Add a JWT interceptor that attaches the bearer token to platform API calls and not to Fauxnance or third-party calls. \\  \\ Store the token securely and clear it on logout. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # login stores the token and authenticates \\ # interceptor attaches the token to platform requests \\ # interceptor does not attach the token to third-party requests \\ # logout clears the session \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Verify the login flow against the real Auth service end to end.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Route guards protect authenticated routes and redirect unauthenticated users to login. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement a route guard on protected routes. \\  \\ Redirect unauthenticated access to the login screen. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # guard blocks unauthenticated navigation \\ # guard allows authenticated navigation

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Typed API clients are generated from the Sprint 6 and Sprint 8 contracts and consumed by the app. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Generate typed clients from contracts/trade-api.yaml and contracts/auth-api.yaml. \\  \\ Build a service layer that consumes the generated clients.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The login screen submits credentials to the Auth service and shows an error alert on failure. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build LoginComponent with username and password inputs and a login button. \\  \\ Show an error alert on authentication failure and redirect on success. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid credentials log in and redirect \\ # invalid credentials show an error alert \\ # empty fields blocked by validation

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The dashboard shows a welcome banner, cash balance, positions summary and navigation actions. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build DashboardComponent with a balance card and positions summary from the account API. \\  \\ Add navigation buttons to the order ticket and blotter, plus logout. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # balance and positions render from the API \\ # navigation buttons route correctly

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The order ticket places an order via the Trade API, validates before submission, and renders every error code from the catalogue as a readable message. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build OrderTicketComponent with instrument, side (BUY or SELL), quantity (> 0) and price inputs. \\  \\ Submit to the order endpoint and show a success or error message. \\  \\ Handle an order that returns NEW, since execution is asynchronous from Sprint 7. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid order submits and shows success \\ # invalid quantity blocked by validation \\ # business-rule rejection shows the mapped error message \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Add a Playwright test covering the place-order journey end to end.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The blotter lists orders with formatted dates, coloured side, values and status badges, and handles an order sitting at NEW. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build BlotterComponent rendering the order table from the order-history API. \\  \\ Format dates, colour BUY green and SELL red, and show status badges (New, Filled, Rejected, Cancelled). \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # order history renders as expected \\ # empty history handled gracefully

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Unit tests and a Playwright suite covering the login and place-order journeys are green, and no API key or secret is present in the built bundle. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write unit tests for components, services and pipes. \\  \\ Write Playwright tests for the login and place-order journeys. \\  \\ Confirm the production bundle contains no API key or secret. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Judge coverage on risk and meaning, not as a percentage.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A preferences service persists a notification channel and display settings per account and applies them at next login. \\ * The service verifies the platform JWT itself and scopes every read and write to the authenticated account. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Build this extension first: Customer Notifications and Watchlists both depend on it. \\ * It consumes nothing from Kafka; it is a plain CRUD service read by other services over HTTP. \\ * Security focus: broken access control (A01), personal contact data (A02), and keeping the internal resolve endpoint off the public path (A05).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service is scaffolded with its own port and repository path, and verifies the JWT on every route. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Scaffold the service and its own preference store. \\  \\ Verify the platform JWT and compare its accountId claim against the path parameter on every route. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Do not trust an upstream service to have checked the token; verify it here.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A customer sets a notification channel and a display currency and both persist across a restart. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement PUT /api/v1/preferences/{accountId}/notifications for the channel choice (email, SMS, push or a combination). \\  \\ Implement PUT /api/v1/preferences/{accountId}/display for base currency, theme and layout. \\  \\ Persist one preference record per account. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # preferences saved and retrieved \\ # preferences survive a service restart \\ # another account's preferences are rejected, not returned empty \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Do not store a copy of anything accounts already owns, such as the holder name; contact data is personal (A02).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * GET /api/v1/preferences/{accountId}/notifications returns the resolved channel for other services to call. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement the resolve endpoint returning the channel and contact detail. \\  \\ Keep the internal read endpoint off the public customer-facing path, or behind a service-to-service credential. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Customer Notifications calls this on the path that gates whether a notification is sent, so favour a small, reliable API.

Summary: Apply Preferences at Next Login & Access-Control Tests
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Stored preferences are applied at the customer's next login and access control is proven by test. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Apply the default account and channel at next login. \\  \\ Add tests that a request for another account's preferences is rejected. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # preferences applied on login \\ # preferences scoped to the authenticated account

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A notifications service consumes trade-events and delivers a message on the channel Customer Preferences holds. \\ * The service verifies the JWT itself and scopes notification history to the owning account. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Depends on Customer Preferences; build it after Preferences, or stub the preference response behind the same interface while Preferences is built. \\ * Consume trade-events, group notification-service; a rejection is as newsworthy as a fill. \\ * Security focus: access control on history (A01), no credential in a payload (A09), and idempotency keyed on eventId.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service consumes trade-events in group notification-service and handles ORDER_FILLED, ORDER_REJECTED and ORDER_CANCELLED. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Scaffold the service with its own port and repository path. \\  \\ Consume trade-events in group notification-service and branch on eventType. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Confirm the consumer group identifier is not shared with any other service.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Before sending, the service calls Customer Preferences to resolve the channel rather than using a hardcoded default. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Call GET /api/v1/preferences/{accountId}/notifications to resolve the channel. \\  \\ Route to the resolved channel; a logging stub is acceptable for a channel the team cannot provision, provided the routing decision is real. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # channel resolved from Customer Preferences and honoured \\ # changing the preference changes the channel used \\ # no notification sent when the preference disables it \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A notification cannot be routed without a channel; this is the hard dependency on Customer Preferences.

Summary: Deliver on Preferred Channel & Track Delivery State
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Delivery state (queued, sent, failed) is tracked separately from consumption state. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Commit the Kafka offset after the notification is durably queued, not after external delivery confirms. \\  \\ Track delivery state so an external channel outage does not stall the partition. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # notification queued and delivery state recorded \\ # external channel outage does not stall the consumer \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A notification payload must never carry a credential or anything kafka-topics.md prohibits from a payload (A09).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A replayed event does not send a second notification, and the owning account can read its history. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Key idempotency on the envelope eventId so a duplicate delivery is a no-op. \\  \\ Implement GET /api/v1/notifications/{accountId} and POST /api/v1/notifications/{accountId}/read, scoped to the JWT account. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # replaying a consumed event does not send a second notification \\ # history read only by the owning account

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A watchlist service consumes market-data, lets customers track instruments, and raises threshold alerts. \\ * A triggered alert reaches Customer Notifications over HTTP and respects the customer's stored channel preference. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Build this last of the three dependent extensions: its alerting depends on Customer Notifications, which depends on Customer Preferences. \\ * Consume market-data, group watchlist-service; do not consume trade-events or orders. A watchlist entry is not a position. \\ * An alert written only to a log has not met the acceptance criterion; it must be delivered through Notifications. \\ * Security focus: access control per account (A01) and a per-account alert cap against denial of service (A04).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service consumes market-data in group watchlist-service and verifies the JWT on every request. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Scaffold the service with its own port and repository path. \\  \\ Consume market-data in group watchlist-service; do not consume trade-events.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A customer creates a watchlist, adds an instrument, and sees its live price. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement POST /api/v1/watchlists and GET /api/v1/watchlists/{id}. \\  \\ Implement POST /api/v1/watchlists/{id}/instruments and DELETE /api/v1/watchlists/{id}/instruments/{symbol}. \\  \\ Read instruments and positions by symbol reference only, never duplicated. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # watchlist created and scoped to the authenticated account \\ # instrument added and its live price shown \\ # instrument removed

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A price alert has a threshold and a direction, and a quote crossing it triggers exactly once per the stated re-arm rule. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement POST /api/v1/alerts, GET /api/v1/alerts and DELETE /api/v1/alerts/{id}. \\  \\ Check each market-data quote against active thresholds; define and document the re-arm behaviour. \\  \\ Cap alerts per account so the market-data consumer cannot be turned into a denial-of-service vector. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # threshold breach triggers an alert \\ # no alert below the threshold \\ # alerts scoped to the authenticated account \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * An alert on an instrument the customer does not hold still works: watchlists are independent of positions.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A triggered alert reaches Customer Notifications over HTTP, end to end, respecting the channel set in Customer Preferences. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Call Customer Notifications when a threshold is crossed. \\  \\ Confirm the notification is delivered on the configured channel, not written to a log. \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Set a channel preference, set a price alert, publish a crossing quote, and confirm the notification arrives on the configured channel with no step stubbed.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A Portfolio and P&L service implements contracts/portfolio-api.yaml, pricing positions from Fauxnance and computing realised and unrealised P&L. \\ * The service verifies the platform JWT and is read-only on the shared trading schema. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Independent of the other three extensions and safe to build in parallel at any point. \\ * It reads accounts, instruments and positions read-only and owns only its realised P&L ledger built from trade-events. \\ * Never call Fauxnance from the browser; the key stays server-side.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service is scaffolded on its own port and verifies the JWT, comparing the accountId claim against the path. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Scaffold the Spring Boot service on port 8081 with its own repository path. \\  \\ Verify the platform JWT and reject a claim that does not match the addressed account with ACC-403.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * GET /api/v1/portfolio/{accountId}/positions returns each holding priced from a live Fauxnance quote. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Read quantity and average cost from positions, read-only. \\  \\ Price via Fauxnance GET /quotes?symbols=... batched and cached for ten seconds. \\  \\ Return 503 with MKT-503 when pricing is unavailable for every held instrument. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # positions priced from a live quote \\ # cached quote reused within the cache window \\ # MKT-503 returned when pricing is unavailable for every symbol

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A realised P&L ledger owned by this service is accumulated from trade-events, idempotently. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Consume trade-events and record realised P&L on each ORDER_FILLED as (executedPrice - averageCostAfter) x quantity on a SELL. \\  \\ Make portfolio_realised_pnl.event_id the primary key so a replay is a no-op. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # realised P&L recorded for a known SELL fill \\ # replayed event does not double-count \\ # P&L computed correctly for a known trade set \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Weighted average cost is fixed by database-schema.sql; this service must agree with the Trade Executor, not pick FIFO or LIFO.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * GET /api/v1/portfolio/{accountId} and /pnl return summary totals converted to the base currency, marking partial results. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement the summary and pnl endpoints returning consolidated holdings and realised versus unrealised P&L. \\  \\ Convert totals to portfolio.base-currency using Fauxnance FX pairs, for example FX:INRUSD. \\  \\ When no FX quote is available for a held currency, exclude that contribution and set partial to true. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # summary total converted to the base currency \\ # realised versus unrealised split correct \\ # missing FX quote sets partial to true rather than failing

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Access control is proven and the calculation is covered by unit tests. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add tests that an account cannot read another account's portfolio. \\  \\ Cover the P&L calculator and the quote cache. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # unauthorised access rejected \\ # quote cache returns a cached value within the window

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The four mandatory extensions are integrated end to end against live data, with one combined OWASP security review and a committed decision log. \\ * The showcase narrative covers the platform, the extensions, design decisions, Copilot usage and the code-quality story. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The four mandatory extensions are Portfolio and P&L, Customer Preferences, Customer Notifications, and Watchlists and Price Alerts, built in that dependency order. \\ * Trade Advice and Signals and Automated Strategy Execution are recommended but not mandatory for this run; no epic is planned for them.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The four extensions and their build order are confirmed on day one with an agreed integration plan. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Confirm the four mandatory extensions and how each plugs into the platform. \\  \\ Agree the backlog, task allocation and integration checkpoints, respecting the Preferences then Notifications then Watchlists order.

Summary: End-to-End Integration Across the Four Extensions
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The customer-facing chain works against live data: a preference drives a notification, and a watchlist alert is delivered on the same channel. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Integrate Customer Preferences, Customer Notifications and Watchlists as one chain. \\  \\ Integrate Portfolio and P&L in parallel and confirm each service authenticates with the platform JWT. \\  \\ Demonstrate the feature working against live data, not fixtures. \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Run the end-to-end chain: set a channel preference, trigger a watchlist alert, and confirm the notification arrives on the configured channel.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * One combined OWASP security review covers the four new services and findings are addressed before the showcase. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Review authorisation, input validation and secure inter-service calls across the four services. \\  \\ Remediate findings and confirm each service verifies the JWT itself.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The extensions pass the SonarQube quality gate and an architecture decision log is committed. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Run SonarQube and address quality-gate findings. \\  \\ Log the architecture decisions and the reasoning behind each significant choice.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The showcase narrative is prepared and rehearsed for the platform demonstration. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Prepare and rehearse the showcase: the platform, the four extensions, design decisions, Copilot usage and code quality. \\  \\ Confirm the demonstration runs against live services. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * For this run the platform demonstration and assessment happen in this taught block; the cloud deployment is assessed separately in the alumni week.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Angular build is deployed to a private S3 bucket behind CloudFront, with an automated build, upload and invalidate cycle. \\ * Direct S3 access is denied, origin access control is configured, and authenticated flows are verified against the deployed front end. \\ * The deployed link is shared with the cohort and assessed asynchronously against the criteria. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * This week runs after the nine-week taught programme, delivered by Fidelity with alumni support; Neueda supplies the material and acceptance criteria only. \\ * It is four and a half days and must run from a printed runbook with no live Neueda support, so every step is tested end to end before delivery. \\ * AWS scope is IAM, the AWS CLI, S3 and CloudFront only; nothing else. \\ * There is no separate final showcase here: the platform demonstration and assessment happened in Sprint 9. \\ * Security focus: private S3 reachable only via CloudFront, IAM least privilege, TLS enforced, no long-lived keys committed (OWASP A05).

Summary: Docker Compose Review & AWS Account / IAM Basics
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The local Docker Compose stack passes its own tests and an IAM user or role is scoped to the bucket and distribution only. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Review the Docker Compose stack as the deployment prerequisite. \\  \\ Set up the AWS account, select a region, and apply a least-privilege IAM policy with no long-lived keys committed.

Summary: AWS CLI Setup & S3 Static Hosting
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The AWS CLI is authenticated and the Angular production build is uploaded to a private S3 bucket. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Configure and authenticate the AWS CLI and verify access. \\  \\ Produce the Angular production build and upload the artefacts to the S3 bucket.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A CloudFront distribution serves the app over HTTPS and the S3 bucket returns access denied when addressed directly. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Configure origin access control so the bucket is not publicly readable, not a public bucket policy. \\  \\ Stand up a CloudFront distribution with the S3 origin and enforce TLS and HTTPS. \\  \\ Confirm direct S3 access is denied while CloudFront access works.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The build, upload and invalidate cycle is a single script or GitHub Actions workflow that runs cleanly from a fresh checkout. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write a deployment script or workflow covering build, upload and cache invalidation. \\  \\ Verify a clean run from a fresh checkout.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Authenticated flows are verified end to end against the deployed front end. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Load the deployed app via CloudFront and complete the login and place-order journeys. \\  \\ Confirm tokens and protected routes behave correctly in production. \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Run an end-to-end check of the authenticated journey against the live deployment.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The deployed link is shared with the cohort and assessed asynchronously against the acceptance criteria. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Share the CloudFront link with the cohort. \\  \\ Confirm the deployment meets each acceptance criterion for the alumni week. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The live platform demonstration to the panel already happened in Sprint 9; this week is assessed on the deployment alone.
